The identical matters in a bunch of cases leading of which is First Appeal No.56 of 2006; Lucknow Development Authority Vs. Vs. Smt. entities.text: Lucknow Development Authority Vs. Vs. Smt. Bhagwan Das and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The order dated October 10, 2017 is extracted here-in-below:-

" Since all the aforesaid first appeals and cross objections arise out of the same award and judgment of the reference court, therefore, all the appeals and cross objections are being decided together by a common judgment.
The land in question was acquired for Sitapur Road Scheme.
The notification under Section 4 of the land acquisition was made on 12.11.1981 while the notification under Section 6 was made on 03.12.1981.
The possession was taken on 15.03.1985 and the Special Land Acquisition Officer made the award on 23.09.1986 awarding compensation @ rupees 1.22 per square feet.
It is not disputed that the entire land under all these appeals is situated in village Sikandarpur Pargana and Tahsil District Lucknow.

The land holders whose land was acquired, feeling aggrieved by the award of the Special land Acquisition Officer preferred reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act which was decided on 03.12.2005.
The learned reference court enhanced the compensation from rupees 1.22 per square feet to rupees 2.17 per square feet.

The land holders were also awarded thirty per cent solatium alongwith interest @ nine per cent for a period of one year from the date of taking over possession and thereafter @ fifteen per cent till the date of payment.

The Lucknow Development Authority has preferred the above noted appeals, feeling aggrieved by the judgment of the reference court while the land holders have preferred cross objection for further enhancement of the award, according to the market value of the acquired land alongwith other consequential benefits.

During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the respondents/land holders has drawn attention of the Court towards a judgment of the reference court dated 24.10.2008 passed in Miscellaneous Case Nos.191 and 123 of 1990.

The submission of the learned counsel is that the land in the aforesaid two miscellaneous cases was also of the same village and the learned reference court has enhanced the quantum of compensation from rupees 1.22 per square feet to rupees 3.25 per square feet.

He has made a prayer that the appeals filed by the Lucknow Development Authority be dismissed and their cross objections be allowed to the extent that they may also be awarded compensation at the same rate.
A copy of the judgment dated 24.10.2010 referred to above, has been placed on record alongwith cross objections.

entities.text: Lucknow Development Authority Throu ... vs Mahaveer Deceased Throu Legal Heirs
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Sri Ajai Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the Lucknow Development Authority has not disputed the fact that in respect of the same land, the reference court has determined the quantum of compensation @ rupees 3.25 per square feet and the same has not been challenged.

In this view of the matter, I am of the view that the cross objectors and the respondents in all the aforesaid first appeals, are also entitled to get compensation at the same rate which the other land holders have been awarded.

In the result, the first appeals no.56, 55, 128, 124 and 126 of 2006 filed by the Lucknow Development Authority are dismissed and cross objections no.38 and 37 of 2006, 10 and 11 of 2007 and 7 of 2008 filed by the objectors are allowed and the market value of the land acquired is fixed at the rate of rupees 3.25 per square feet.
The objectors shall be entitled to get compensation at the rate of rupees 3.25 per square feet instead of rupees 2.17 per square feet.
They shall also be entitled to get twelve per cent interest with effect from the date of acquisition till the date of possession alongwith solatium at the rate of thirty per cent.

They shall also be entitled to get interest at the rate of nine per cent per annum for a period of one year from the date of taking over possession of the land and thereafter interest at the rate of fifteen per cent per annum till the date of payment."
4. Learned counsel for the appellant does not dispute the aforesaid and submits that the appeal may be decided in terms of the aforesaid order.
5. In view of above, the appeal is hereby dismissed.
No order as to costs.
